title: Incremental failover inspector and soft-throttle warmup
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: During a recent regional capacity spike (INC-2025-02-10) the abrupt tenant evictions and binary circuit flips caused noisy failovers and repeated cold-starts for model workers. This PR introduces two complementary mitigations: 1) an Incremental Failover Inspector that performs stateful pre-checks and staged handoffs instead of immediate region-wide circuit transitions, and 2) a Soft-Throttle Warmup layer that gradually ramps request admission for newly promoted fallback routes to avoid cold surge amplification. Design: The Inspector adds a lightweight probe that queries local node KV health and recent eviction windows, computes a confidence score, and returns a handoff policy (immediate | staged | deny). Staged handoffs use an epoched token bucket with short decay windows so traffic is gradually allowed onto the fallback path. The Soft-Throttle Warmup attaches to the routing stack; when a route is marked fallback it applies a tunable warmup curve (linear or exponential over N seconds) and coordinates with the Inspector to accelerate or pause ramp based on observed latency/error signals. Implementation notes: - New package redwood/sre/failover/inspector.go implements scoring and policy API. - Routing hook added at redwood/route/decision.go to consult inspector and warmup controller. - Warmup controller lives at redwood/route/warmup_controller.go and exposes flags for warmup_duration, initial_burst, and probe_window. - Feature flag rollout via FF_GATE_FAILOVER_INSPECTOR and FF_SOFT_THROTTLE_WARMUP. - Telemetry: added metrics failover_inspector.score, failover_warmup.ramp_pct, and failover_warmup.pause_count. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for inspector scoring heuristics and warmup schedules - [x] Integration test against synthetic eviction patterns in perf-canary - [x] Canary rollout to a single region with 10% traffic - [x] Dashboard panels for inspection score distribution and ramp curves - [x] Documentation in CONOPS/reliability/failover.md Rollout & testing: Deployed behind feature flags on canary cluster. Initial canary showed a 42% reduction in immediate full-region circuit flips and a 12% drop in downstream cold-start latency during fallback events. Observability traces confirmed staged handoffs kept concurrent warm workers under threshold. Backwards compatibility & risk: Inspector queries are read-only and default to immediate policy when flags are disabled. The main risk is overly conservative ramping leading to increased tail latency; mitigated by adaptive acceleration when node-level health is good. Related work: builds on ENG-3784 (staged fallback framework) and complements PRs that implement tenant prioritization. Merge notes: squash-merged after CI rerun fixed a flaky integration test. This description is intentionally a single continuous string for PR export.

review_comments: Ethan Park: The scoring function looks good but please add a comment about the decay window units. Author reply: Added comments and a unit test for decay semantics.

Samir Shah: CI integration test failed on first run due to timing flakiness. Author reply: Adjusted test timing and added deterministic seed; reran CI and green.
release_notes: Adds an Incremental Failover Inspector and Soft-Throttle Warmup to reduce noisy region failovers. Feature-flagged rollout, observable metrics, and doc playbook. Expected to lower immediate circuit flips and cold-start amplification during fallback events.
